subject: gender-studies
intro: Gender studies trains people to see how identity, power and institutions interact — a lens that leads into social services, human resources, social research and rights-focused law.

roles.title: Child, Family, and School Social Workers
roles.what: Provide social services to improve the social and psychological functioning of children and their families — assisting parents, arranging adoptions and foster homes, and in schools addressing problems from truancy to crisis, while advising teachers.
roles.where: Units 5 and 7 — care work and unpaid labour, violence and the legal system — explain the family stresses these social workers meet; unit 1's concepts of gender and identity ground work with children and families in the course's own terms.

roles.title: Human Resources Specialists
roles.what: Recruit, screen, interview and place people in organisations, and handle the surrounding work — training, workplace policies, and the pay and fairness questions that shape how staff are hired and treated.
roles.where: Unit 5's labour markets and the wage gap speak directly to hiring and pay decisions; unit 6's media and representation informs employer branding and recruitment; unit 4's intersectionality grounds fair-treatment and inclusion policy.

roles.title: Sociologists
roles.what: Study human society and social behaviour — examining the groups and institutions people form, tracing their origin and growth, and analysing how group activities shape the lives of individual members.
roles.where: The course is applied sociology of gender: units 1 to 4 supply the concepts — sex and gender, intersectionality, queer theory — and unit 5's wage-gap and care-work topics are exactly the labour-market questions sociologists quantify.

roles.title: Lawyers
roles.what: Represent clients in criminal and civil litigation and other legal proceedings, draw up legal documents, and advise clients — some specialising in fields such as family, employment, discrimination or human rights law.
roles.where: Unit 7 is the direct match — reproductive rights and law, violence and the legal system, global feminist politics — and unit 5's topics on wage gaps and gendered labour feed discrimination and workplace cases.
